audit.summary: Two exact admissible quadratic trajectories establish IGMM loop nontermination and false OGMM ESP certification; a separate LRSP objective/gradient mismatch is locally established. Checked lower-bound construction not refuted.
limitations: P1 — Fixed previous-step backtracking can loop forever — Counterevidence: An exact solve could avoid this example, but exactness is not required for IGMM. The narrower experimental subsolver does not replace the general algorithm contract. x1 is not an optimum.

P2 — Missing tau term permits false normalized ESP — Counterevidence: Read routine e as input ebar. No rounding or approximate-QP explanation. A cannot consistently mean A+tau elsewhere. The example is not a violation of the function-error rate: f(x2)=1/32.

P3 — Printed LRSP objective and gradient differ — Counterevidence: They coincide for A^T1=0; that is not the stated Gaussian-design restriction. A sign typo in the objective is a plausible explanation.

proposition.claim:
The source assumes a finite-dimensional real space with norm \(\|x\|^2=\langle Bx,x\rangle\), \(B\succ0\), and a convex differentiable full-domain function with \(L_f\)-Lipschitz gradient and a nonempty minimizer set (p. 2). For records \((z_i,f_i,g_i)\), define \[\ell_i(y)=f_i+\langle g_i,y-z_i\rangle,\qquad
 \phi_i(y,g)=\ell_i(y)+\frac{\|g-g_i\|_*^2}{2L_f}.\] The proposed bound is \(p(y)=\min_g\max_i\phi_i(y,g)\). The smooth convex interpolation inequality gives \(\phi_i(y,\nabla f(y))\le f(y)\), and therefore \(\max_i\ell_i(y)\le p(y)\le f(y)\). Writing \(G=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) and \(c_i=\langle g_i,z_i\rangle-f_i-\|g_i\|_*^2/(2L_f)\) gives \[p(y)=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}
 \left\{\langle G\lambda,y\rangle-\langle c,\lambda\rangle
              -\frac{\|G\lambda\|_*^2}{2L_f}\right\}.\] Its conjugate is a \(1/L_f\)-strongly convex quadratic plus the convex value function \(\min\{\langle c,\lambda\rangle:\lambda\in\Delta_m,\ G\lambda=s\}\), extended by \(+\infty\) outside \(\operatorname{conv}(G)\). This supports smoothness. At \(z_i\), the value sandwich forces \(p(z_i)=f_i\); differentiability and tangency of \(f-p\ge0\) give \(\nabla p(z_i)=g_i\). This contact argument supplies the meaningful reading of the gradient sandwich in Proposition 2.6. No substantive defect in these checked lower-bound conclusions is established.

For both algorithmic examples take \[E=\mathbb R,\quad B=1,\quad f(x)=x^2/2,\quad L_f=1,\quad
 L=2,\quad \tau=1/2,\quad x_0=1.\] This function is convex and differentiable on all of \(\mathbb R\), its gradient has Lipschitz constant 1, and its minimizer is \(x^*=0\). The algorithms expressly permit \(L\ge L_f\).

Location: Algorithm 3.1 p.12 line 21; arbitrary-quality solver p.11; rate (3.7) p.13

Paraphrase: Backtracking plus fallback produces IGMM iterates even for arbitrary-quality feasible QP approximations.
